newsitem.title: UK: Orange shares firm after subscriber update.
newsitem.headline: Orange shares firm after subscriber update.

text.p: Shares in Orange Plc edged higher in pre-market trading on Monday after the mobile phone operator issued an upbeat statement on growth in subscriber numbers and market share in 1996.
The stock was up 1-1/2p at 189-1/2 by 0806 GMT.

Analysts said the statement was in line with their expectations for the company, which was listed on the London exchange in March last year and subsequently joined the FTSE 100 index despite never having made a profit.

"The subscriber numbers were marginally below what we had expected but there is a higher proportion of high-use business users, so overall the statement is in line with expectations," said Steve Scruton, an analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing.
"As long as the company keeps growing in line with expectations it should be fine holding the shares," he added.
In its statement Orange said subscriber numbers more than doubled in 1996 to over 785,000, while market share rose to 11.5 percent at the end of 1996 from seven percent a year before.
Group managing director Hans Snook said it had been another record year for Orange. "We stay right on our plan for growth of subscribers, market share, usage, network coverage and churn."
